subject.title: fix: doctor upgrade 7.2-beta.1 - 7.2-beta.2 fails on fractional restart handoffs

question: Should the project accept deleting expired restart handoffs and flooring live legacy fractional trace timestamps as the upgrade policy for the beta.1-to-STRICT migration?
rationale: The patch is mechanically focused and proof-backed, but the choice to discard expired state and canonicalize live persisted values is a product/data-migration policy that cannot be inferred from automated checks alone.

options.title: Accept the bounded migration policy
options.body: Merge the repair with its current tests and package-upgrade evidence, treating restart handoffs as transient state whose valid timing representation is integer milliseconds.

options.title: Pause for a different retention policy
options.body: Keep the PR open if maintainers require retaining expired handoffs or a different conversion rule before the generic STRICT migration.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded migration policy
recommendation.body: Merge the repair with its current tests and package-upgrade evidence, treating restart handoffs as transient state whose valid timing representation is integer milliseconds.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete regression, migration rationale, and real package-upgrade evidence needed to answer the intended policy boundary.
